content.caption: TikTok — oEmbed html always ships an inline <script>; it is stripped and embed.js is injected instead. This is the bug from issue #45.
embedCode wins over oembed.html — the pin below comes from the pasted snippet, not from the (deliberately broken) oEmbed html.
Pinterest — pasted embedCode with no url at all: PinUtils.build() upgrades the anchor, and the fallback card would render as a <div>, never an empty <a>.

oembed.html: <iframe src="https://www.linkedin.com/embed/feed/update/urn%3Ali%3Aactivity%3A7282719529426636800" height="600" width="100%" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen title="Embedded LinkedIn post"></iframe>

content.caption: LinkedIn — self-contained iframe, the one platform with no widget script; the iframe keeps loading="lazy". Renders only for posts LinkedIn serves publicly.
Instagram — pasted embedCode carrying the inline embed.js tag (stripped, then injected). Instagram serves embeds only for public posts.
Facebook — fb-post markup driven by FB.XFBML.parse(). Facebook renders it only for apps it recognises, so without an app id it stays blank.
Fallback — nothing but a url: a single "View on X" line, with no provider line repeating it.
